content.comment_body: Hi [user_name], I need your assistance again regarding the program. The logic you previously provided manages the positioning cylinder’s location. Currently, everything works, except the relay output keeps switching on and off when the analog input value fluctuates slightly around the setpoint (for example, between 99 and 101). I understand analog signals can be unstable in this narrow range. I’d like to add a dead band so that the relay output does not energize unnecessarily when the actual value is close to the setpoint and minor changes occur. The output from the PLC should stay OFF within this range. Please advise how I can implement this. Providing a simple example for programming dead band logic would be helpful — I can adapt your example into the existing program version you shared earlier. Thank you in advance. -------------------------------------------------------- Split from Analog input programming.
You can add either an ON delay or OFF delay before activating the output. Setting a delay of about 1–2 seconds usually works well. Sent from App

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience issues with relay output instability, as analog input fluctuations around the setpoint cause the relay to switch rapidly. This creates unpredictability in system behavior. Users expect enhanced control logic—such as implementing a dead band or output delays—to provide more reliable and consistent relay operation in response to analog inputs near threshold values.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the relay output to remain steady and avoid repeated activation or deactivation when the analog input is within a small deviation around the setpoint. They are looking for a straightforward dead band logic example or a built-in function to achieve this stable performance.
